🚀 Join the Future of Commerce with Whatnot!
Whatnot is the largest live shopping platform in North America and Europe to buy, sell, and discover the things you love. Whether it's trading cards, fashion, electronics, or live plants, our sellers are building real businesses across hundreds of categories. We're building live commerce at a scale that's never been done in the West, and there's no playbook to copy. The people here are shaping how an entirely new industry develops.
As a remote co-located team, we're inspired by our values and anchored in hubs across the US, UK, Ireland, Poland, Germany, and Australia. We move fast, stay close to our users, and focus on the work that drives the most impact.
We're one of the fastest growing marketplaces and were recently named the #1 Best Startup Employer in America by Forbes. Check out the latest Whatnot updates on our news and engineering blogs and join us as we enable anyone to turn their passion into a business and bring people together through commerce.
💻 Role
Enterprise Engineering supports the needs of our largest and most complex sellers. As sellers grow their businesses on Whatnot, their needs evolve—and this team builds the systems and tooling to support them at scale.
Enterprise is looking for their next software engineer who will operate at the intersection of engineering and customer success—working directly with enterprise sellers and their technical teams to design, implement, and support custom integrations on top of Whatnot’s APIs and infrastructure. Unlike a traditional software engineering role, you’ll have a direct line to the customers using what you build. You’ll spend your time writing code, building internal tooling, automating repetitive support workflows, developing integrations, and identifying product gaps that can be solved once instead of manually worked around hundreds of times.
This role is ideal for a software engineer who wants to transition into a more customer-facing role
, partnering directly with enterprise sellers and their engineering teams to help them successfully adopt live commerce. You’ll build integrations, tooling, and scalable technical solutions that make onboarding and operating on Whatnot seamless, while helping shape how we support the next generation of enterprise sellers as our platform continues to grow.
The Role Entails
Partnering directly with enterprise sellers and their engineering teams to architect and implement bespoke integrations leveraging Whatnot’s APIs and platform capabilities.
Acting as the technical bridge between customers and internal teams—translating seller needs into scalable solutions while collaborating closely with engineering, product, and account management stakeholders.
Building durable tooling, workflows, and support infrastructure that help scale enterprise onboarding, integration support, and long-term customer success, including hands-on coding focused on developing scalable integration solutions and internal operational tooling.
Solving complex post-sale technical challenges while helping define how Whatnot supports enterprise commerce moving forward.
We offer flexibility to work from home or from one of our global office hubs, and we value in-person time for planning, problem-solving, and connection. Team members in this role must live within commuting distance of our Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York or Seattle hub.
👋 You
People who do well at Whatnot tend to be comfortable figuring things out as they go, biased toward action, and genuinely curious about what they're building. They care more about outcomes than credit and stay close to the product and the people using it.
As our next engineer on Enterprise, you should have 3+ years of software engineering experience, plus:
Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science or related field or equivalent work experience.
Ability to work with customers directly, both satiating customer expectations as well and ensuring internal company strategic standards and goals are met.
Comfort talking to customers directly. You can run a technical conversation with an external engineering team, ask the questions that surface the real requirement, and say no when the right answer is a platform fix rather than a one-off.
Ability to flexibly work across multiple workstreams, thriving in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to understand complex customer success workflows and envision and build tooling to better support our bespoke system.
Strong grounding in APIs, distributed systems, and data synchronization — you've debugged something gnarly across a system boundary you didn't control.
A track record of automating away work rather than absorbing it. You get uncomfortable doing the same manual fix twice.
Ability to take ownership of an ambiguous area, define it, and drive impact — this role has no playbook yet.
Experience with e-commerce or operational systems (Shopify, ChannelAdvisor, Magento, NetSuite, ShipStation, WMS/ERP platforms) is a plus.
🎁 Benefits
Flexible Time off Policy and Company-wide Holidays (including a spring and winter break)
Health Insurance options including Medical, Dental, Vision
Work From Home Support
Home office setup allowance
Monthly allowance for cell phone and internet
Care benefits
Monthly allowance for wellness
Annual allowance towards Childcare
Lifetime benefit for family planning, such as adoption or fertility expenses
Retirement; 401k offering for Traditional and Roth accounts in the US (employer match up to 4% of base salary) and Pension plans internationally
Monthly allowance to dogfood the app
All Whatnauts are expected to develop a deep understanding of our product. We're passionate about building the best user experience, and all employees are expected to use Whatnot as both a buyer and a seller as part of their job (our dogfooding budget makes this fun and easy!).
Parental Leave
16 weeks of paid parental leave + one month gradual return to work *company leave allowances run concurrently with country

It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.
About The Role
New York Times Conversion helps customers understand subscription benefits from NYT's US, International news and standalone applications through to the purchase and onboarding flows. The team consists of engineers, designers, data analysts and product managers focusing on shipping user-centered, experiment-driven features.
As a Full Stack Software engineer on Conversion, your work will have a directly quantifiable impact on the bottom line of the Times, ensuring the work of our world-leading journalists. You will engineer features across desktop and mobile that promote understanding of subscription benefits no matter where they are in the user experience. Web Conversion approaches this by optimizing conversion surfaces through sales, free trial and directing users to high value surfaces such as native apps.
You will work in React and TypeScript on the frontend, Node.js for web applications, and Go-based APIs, all running on the AWS cloud platform. You will help develop, test, and operate features end-to-end, from idea to production, alongside a collaborative team that values learning and continuous improvement.
We value collaboration, transparency and openness, diversity, learning, community and continuous improvement. Our team builds great things through collaboration with other team members and with our partners on platform teams. You will report to the Engineering Manager of the Subscription Conversion team.
Responsibilities
Contribute directly to our mission of reaching 15+ million paid subscriptions by 2027
Build the conversion funnel for NYT customers, working across NYT platforms and services
Improve the payment workflows for digital and print subscriptions
Work with design, data, marketing and other collaborators to have a measurable impact on the NYT's business
Participate in design reviews, code reviews and A/B test brainstorms
Participate in an on-call rotation for the systems you help build.
Partner with Project, Product, Design and Engineering Management to build and release projects
Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
Basic Qualifications
2+ years of full-time software engineering experience building and supporting user-facing features in large-scale web applications using TypeScript and modern frontend frameworks such as React
Experience in version control tools (i.e Git)
Familiarity with server-side web development (for example, Node.js, Go, or a similar language), or a clear interest in learning it
Experience collaborating with designers, product managers, and other engineers to ship features
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with A/B testing or experimentation platforms
Prior experience working on consumer-facing or subscription products
Prior experience working on sales or growth programs, such as revenue-focused features, funnels, or acquisition/retention projects
Additional Compensation And Benefits
For roles in the U.S., dependent on your role, you may be eligible for variable pay, such as an annual bonus and restricted stock. Benefits may include medical, dental and vision benefits, Flexible Spending Accounts (F.S.A.s), a company-matching 401(k) plan, employee stock purchase plan, paid vacation, paid sick days, paid parental leave, tuition reimbursement and professional development programs.
For roles outside of the U.S., information on benefits will be provided during the interview process.

OUR PHILOSOPHY
We are champions of our investors' goals and stewards of founders' dreams, but more than that, we are ethical, honest partners who serve, educate, and protect our founders and investors. We take on the challenges and complex conversations because we operate out of integrity and genuine care.
About The Role
BIP Capital's technology team is hiring a Junior AI Engineer to help bring large language models into the day to day work of an investment platform. You'll work directly with a Senior AI Engineer to add AI capabilities to our existing full-stack applications, and to design and ship retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, agentic workflows, and prompt-engineered LLM pipelines that real investment and operations teams rely on. This is an apprenticeship-style role built for someone early in their career who is a strong full-stack engineer first and genuinely curious about applied AI. You will not be expected to own architecture on day one. You will be expected to execute well, learn quickly, and take real work off the Senior AI Engineer's plate within your first few months

Hybrid / On-site (In-office Wednesdays).
What You'll Do
Add AI capabilities to our existing full-stack applications: new LLM-powered features, workflows, and interfaces built directly into the products our investment and operations teams already use
Build and improve RAG systems with a Senior AI Engineer, from chunking and embedding strategies through retrieval quality and evaluation
Manage context windows and model inputs: decide what information a model actually needs, how to structure it, and when a task calls for a different model or a multi-modal approach across text, documents, and images
Help design agentic workflows when the problem calls for it, including multi-step LLM pipelines, tool use, and orchestration
Prompt-engineer and evaluate LLM workflows, treating prompts and retrieval as things you measure rather than guess at
Write clean, testable services and data pipelines that move information reliably between systems
Translate fuzzy workflow needs from investment and operations colleagues into concrete technical problems
Requirements
What we're looking for
We weigh engineering fundamentals and trajectory far more heavily than years of experience or a specific pedigree. This is a product engineering role: we want a full-stack engineer who is genuinely excited about building with large language models, someone who thinks naturally in terms of retrieval, embeddings, context windows, and tool use, and who wants to ship features real people use day to day.
Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science, AI/ML, Engineering, or a related field
Solid software engineering fundamentals in Node.js and TypeScript: REST APIs, async and promise-based concurrency, a testing framework such as Jest or Vitest, and everyday comfort in git. Our front end runs on AWS Amplify, so familiarity there is a plus. Python is a nice to have, especially for RAG and data-heavy work, but it is not our primary stack
Exposure to cloud infrastructure, ideally AWS, including AWS's AI and LLM services such as Bedrock, Bedrock AgentCore, and Knowledge Bases for Bedrock
Practical experience with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar): function calling and tool use, structured outputs, streaming responses, and managing token usage and context window limits
Hands-on experience building something real with LLMs, ideally something you can point to: a project, prototype, or shipped feature you can walk us through, including what broke and how you fixed it
Comfort designing LLM-in-the-loop evaluation and testing pipelines: building golden datasets, using LLM-as-judge scoring, and writing regression tests for prompts and retrieval, with tools such as promptfoo, Braintrust, or Ragas
Comfort with AI native development practices: using tools like Claude Code or Cursor as part of your everyday workflow, not as a novelty

My client, a mid-size private credit firm, is adding the second engineer to its AI data platform team: a net-new seat, not a backfill, reporting directly to the engineer who built the platform now used across the firm.
If you are ready to be the person who builds and ships them into production for a firm that will actually use them, this is the role for you.
What's the Job?
My client has built a production AI platform that supports the firm's investment process including automated investment memo generation, due diligence questionnaire (DDQ) automation, and retrieval over complex financial documents. The business case is document volume: the firm may receive thousands of documents from a company it is underwriting a loan for, and the platform has to read them, summarize them, extract what matters, and generate new documents from what it finds.
You will be the team's second engineer, working alongside its lead and directly with investment, investor relations, and operations professionals. Day to day you will:
Own and extend production AI systems, including the investment memo pipeline, DDQ automation, and the RAG infrastructure over financial documents.
Build provenance tracking, source attribution, and review workflows so investment professionals can verify generated output against source documents.
Build and maintain the platform's agent infrastructure: harnesses, skills, subagents, and tool integrations.
Run projects end to end: design, implementation, deployment, and ongoing production support.
Translate the workflows of non-technical stakeholders into tools they will actually rely on.
Compensation
Base salary of $200,000–$250,000, commensurate with experience, plus a discretionary bonus
Fully paid health, dental, and vision premiums, including dependents
Unlimited PTO, within reason
Qualifications
3–5 years of professional software engineering experience with strong fundamentals in one or more of Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Rust, or Go. There is flexibility on years for an exceptional engineer with a strong track record of shipping.
Minimum: You use AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or similar) as your primary development mode and run development end to end through them including writing, testing, quality, and deployment, with strong judgment about verifying what the model produces.
Better: You have also built AI tools for end users, such as chatbots or LLM-driven automation of business processes.
Best: You have built the platform itself: RAG infrastructure and data ingestion, and the agent layer that sits around the model.
A demonstrated record of independently designing, building, and shipping production software.
Financial services or another document-heavy, compliance-sensitive domain is preferred; vector databases, document parsing, and Anthropic/OpenAI agent SDKs are a plus.
Genuinely strong verbal and written communication. This is a 50-person firm and you will work directly with investment professionals and the COO.
No finance background is required, but this is a finance culture rather than a startup culture, and you should want that.
This is an engineering role. It is not a fit for data scientists or quantitative researchers/analysts.
Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. My client is unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa now or in the future.
Location
New York City, five days a week in the office, with work-from-home Fridays in the summer and flexibility around holiday weeks.
Who are They?
My client is a private credit investment firm with more than $10B in assets under management, providing bespoke credit solutions to stakeholders and management teams of U.S. middle-market companies that need capital for growth, acquisitions, operational challenges, or financial distress. The firm has 50 employees and is currently raising its fourth fund.
The hiring manager spent his career in machine learning at a leading AI software company and a global bank before joining roughly two and a half years ago, and he built the internal platform this role will help scale. The firm has had no voluntary turnover in five years.

Raytheon’s Systems Engineering & Test Capabilities organization is seeking a Systems Engineer II in Huntsville, Alabama to support radar performance analysis activities for missile defense flight test missions. In this role, you will perform radar performance assessments, analyze data from live mission events, develop and implement verification strategies for advanced radar capabilities and software builds, and support systems validation efforts within Hardware‑in‑the‑Loop and other mission-representative environments. You will work both independently and alongside multidisciplinary engineering teams to evaluate sensor behavior, investigate anomalies, and prepare technical findings for internal and external stakeholders.
What You Will Do:
Plan, prepare, and execute radar performance analysis activities supporting live missile defense flight tests, ensuring sensor readiness and alignment with mission objectives.
Analyze radar measurement data collected during flight test events to characterize detection, tracking, discrimination, and overall sensor performance under operationally representative conditions.
Evaluate time‑sensitive radar outputs, including track timelines, track quality, measurement accuracy, and sensor resource usage, to determine compliance with mission and system-level requirements.
Perform pre‑mission analysis using engineering tools and flight‑test simulation environments to predict radar behavior, assess risk areas, and identify expected performance envelopes.
Produce high‑quality technical artifacts including performance reports, engineering briefings, mission analysis summaries, and data packages used to inform leadership, government stakeholders, and mission partners.
Support readiness reviews and mission execution events by presenting radar performance expectations, risk assessments, and post-test analysis plans.
Maintain configuration control of analysis procedures, data pipelines, scripts, and verification artifacts to ensure repeatability, traceability, and compliance with engineering processes.
Ability to travel locally and non-locally to support test activities or customer engagements (as required).
Qualifications You Must Have
Typically requires a degree in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM) and a minimum of 2 years of prior relevant experience.
Experience with scripting and/or software development (MATLAB, Python, C/C++, and/or Linux/Red).
Experience with Systems engineering (example integration, verification and/or system testing).
Qualifications We Prefer
Demonstrated experience in test, integration, or verification and validation of X-Band family of radars, Early Warning Radars or other Missile Defense System sensors.
Experience analyzing Sensor, RF, or radar data, such as time-series measurements, track data, signal returns, resources, or discrimination, using engineering tools.
Experience working in multidisciplinary teams of systems engineering professionals.
Experience with MATLAB, Linux Operating Systems, and Shell scripting for performing integration, verification, and validation test analysis.
Experience interfacing with internal or external customers, providing technical solutions to user requirements, analyzing radar data, and generating and maintaining technical documentation and work instructions.

SECURITY SOFTWARE ENGINEER (STARLINK)
At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and serves millions of users worldwide. We design, build, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites and all of the space-ground infrastructure necessary for a constellation of that size. As we scale the constellation to hundreds of thousands of satellites, and become a foundation of global connectivity both on earth (and in space), we are looking for excellent engineers to help us build secure, defensible systems from the ground up.
Skills
In this role, you will influence the security of software across our space and terrestrial systems. Ideally, you have notable skills in one or more of the following:
Applied cryptography
Network security
Operating system security
Secure/Authenticated boot
Incident response and adversary detection
Vulnerability research
Software engineering
Responsibilities
Design and build security infrastructure for Starlink, including cryptographic services and other security-critical services
Develop security features for Starlink systems, including our router, dish, gateways, and satellites
Design security into factory processes and provide network services in support of this
Maintain existing production systems and improve security posture via both direct implementation and recommendations to other teams
Build prototypes and help identify, design, and test security improvements
Further our mission of providing secure and reliable Internet to underserved communities

Bachelor's degree in computer science or another STEM discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience in security software development in lieu of a degree
Experience with one or more software development languages (i.e. Python, C++, Golang)
Experience designing and implementing security solutions for operating systems, distributed systems, or other enterprise/large-scale infrastructure
Preferred Skills And Experience
Experience contributing security improvements to complex systems
Experience working with special purpose security hardware such as Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs) and Hardware Security Modules (HSMs)
Fundamental understanding of network protocols; including the TCP/IP stack as well as UDP based protocols
Experienced in navigating large, complex, interactive systems
Flexibility, communicating clearly, and establishing and maintaining productive working relationships with other engineering teams
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
Ability to work both independently and in a team
Demonstrated ability to deal with ambiguity and to learn new technologies quickly

We are just beginning to explore Starlink's potential global impact and are seeking top-tier engineers to help maximize its utility for communities and businesses around the globe.
As a Development Test Engineer for Starlink, you will be responsible designing and building “hardware-in-the-loop” (HIL/HITL) test systems. These systems allow for Starlink software engineers to build technologies such as space laser mesh networks, next-generation phased array antennas, advanced collision avoidance algorithms, and much more. You will be working with a multidisciplinary team on efforts such as constructing a platform to simulate the motion profile of mobile customers, performing end-to-end validation of the Starlink network, and simulating ion thruster functionality with/without vacuum. You will also be collaborating closely with internal and external stakeholders to ensure that we provide a highly-effective, user-friendly integrated test platform.
Responsibilities
Design, build, and maintain highly reliable hardware-in-the-loop (HIL/HITL) testbeds—including surrounding infrastructure, tooling, and support equipment—for the Starlink software continuous integration system.
Develop test cases and create simulation environments that replicate on-orbit scenarios to deliver flight-like testing capabilities.
Ensure all software has appropriate level of test coverage, balancing reliability, velocity and safety.
Pioneer innovative strategies to scale the HITL fleet in accordance with the Starlink software organization’s growing test demands.
Analyze and troubleshoot HITL test results to identify testbed issues and prevent software bugs from reaching production.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical, aerospace, or a related engineering discipline.
1+ years of professional test experience within electrical, mechanical, and/or aerospace engineering.
Preferred Skills And Experience
Experience with integration and testing of electrical, electromechanical, RF, and/or propulsion systems.
Experience with electrical test equipment such as oscilloscopes, DAQs, electronic loads, and spectrum analyzers.
Experience with 3D CAD software for design, modeling, and manufacturing applications.
Experience with programmable logic controllers (PLCs).
Experience with communication protocols including USB, VISA, CAN bus, SPI, I2C, and Modbus.
Experience configuring networks and troubleshooting layers 2-4 of the OSI-model.
Strong skills in troubleshooting, debugging, performance optimization, and unit testing.
Solid fundamental knowledge of networks, electronics, RF communications, math, and physics.
Experience with simulation software and data analysis.
Excellent organizational and communication skills.
Ability to learn quickly and work effectively in a dynamic environment.
Additional Requirements
Must be willing to work all shifts, overtime, and/or weekends as needed.
Must be able to lift and carry up to 25 lbs.
Compensation And Benefits
Pay range:
Level I: $105,000.00 - $120,000.00/per year
Level II: $115,000.00 - $145,000.00/per year
Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.
Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees in Washington State accrue paid sick time in compliance with state and federal law.
